narrative.overview:
The video is the hero. Every piece of chrome is a dark, slightly blue-tinted translucent material that floats over the picture and darkens it only where text sits; when no video plays, the ground is a near-black ink. The library surfaces carry the same logic with titles bringing their own colour through full-bleed still backdrops held back by ink scrims. The app has no light theme and never had one: dark surfaces were designed as dark from the start.

The system is built for a 960x540 dp canvas read from a sofa with a D-pad, on a Fire TV Stick 2nd gen whose small GPU shares memory with a 4K decode. Performance is part of the visual language: every surface is drawn in one pass, without offscreen layers, so focus moves and transitions hold frame time. Focus is depth, not colour: the focused thing lifts toward the viewer on a quick, non-bouncing spring and takes the lighter raised layer or a ring. One accent, a clear blue, marks what is playing, what is selected and where focus rings sit on artwork; everything else is neutral.

Type is Inter at a refined ten-foot scale (nothing below 13sp), copy is plain sentence case, and status words carry their meaning by colour on a tint of their own colour.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-native translucent material over video; ink ground when nothing plays.
Depth by tone, lift and scrim; no drop shadows anywhere.
One accent (#3D9BFF), used sparingly; progress in lists is neutral.
Focus springs (0.22s, no overshoot) with scale and ring, read only while drawing.
One-pass drawing on weak hardware; no offscreen layers, the backdrop included.
5% overscan-safe inset (48 x 27 dp); chrome never sits closer to the edge.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue marks state (playing, selected, focused artwork, caret, watched); it never decorates. Progress lines in lists and cards are neutral (text-secondary on track) so the accent stays for focus; only the player's own seek bar fills in accent.

rules.name: The Dark-Native Rule
rules.body: Dark surfaces are designed deliberately as their own scale (ink, night glass, raised slate); never derive them by flipping a light scale. There is no light theme.

rules.name: The Tinted Status Rule
rules.body: A status word sits on a 16% tint of its own colour, so a list of them reads by colour without shouting.

rules.name: The Sofa Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing below 13sp; it is read from across a room.

rules.name: The Tabular Where Needed Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures only on numbers that tick or align (clock times, counts, buffer, bitrate). A font feature makes text layout several times slower on the stick, which a list of rows feels.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No small all-caps line above a heading. Headings stand alone; context goes in a caption line beside or below, in sentence case. All caps is reserved for short status marks (LIVE) and format names (4K, VPN).

rules.name: The One Pass Rule
rules.body: Every surface draws in one pass: rounded fills instead of clips where possible, alpha applied per draw (ModulateAlpha) rather than through an offscreen copy, animated values read in the draw phase so focus moves repaint two items and recompose nothing. The library backdrop bakes its ink scrims into the still once (on the CPU, off the main thread), so its crossfade draws one or two pictures and no layer: the layered version cost the stick ~50 ms a frame.

rules.name: The No Stacked Glass Rule
rules.body: Never stack one translucent surface on another.

rules.name: The Flat Scrim Rule
rules.body: Behind full-height chrome over video, prefer a flat tint under the content and a gradient only where content never reaches; a full-screen gradient cost the stick four times the frame time of a flat tint.

rules.name: The Readable Over White Rule
rules.body: Every scrim is dense enough where text sits that body text clears 4.5:1 over a white sky: the library backdrop holds 94% to 86% ink across the text column (to 75% width) before falling off by 95%, plus a 70% ink band at the top behind Search.

dos: Do pick spacing from the step scale (4 to 48dp) and keep chrome inside the 48 x 27dp safe inset.
Do give focus as lift: raised slate plus the 1.5dp soft white ring on rows and panels, a 3dp accent ring on artwork, on the 0.22s no-overshoot spring.
Do take a theme colour for any focus ring that must stand out, at 3:1 or better against what it sits on.
Do draw every surface in one pass and read animated values in the draw phase.
Do keep text over pictures at 4.5:1 with ink scrims dense where the text sits.
Do draw marks (checks, carets, dots) as shapes in the theme colours.
Do let missing art fall back to raised slate with a monogram or number, at the same size.
donts: Don't add eyebrow labels (a small all-caps line above a heading).
Don't use drop shadows or blur; depth is tone, lift and scrim.
Don't stack translucent surfaces, or add offscreen layers.
Don't use the accent for decoration or for list progress.
Don't set text below 13sp, or apply tabular figures to text that does not tick or align.
Don't let motion overshoot or bounce; a remote carries no momentum.
Don't derive dark surfaces by inverting a light scale.
Don't use typed glyphs as icons.
